Definitions

Quadrant Analysis — Sales × Location Potential

Stores plotted by Actual Sales (X-axis, INR Lakhs) and Location Potential (Y-axis, INR Lakhs, based on catchment/POI/competition). Click on a store dot for the Category Scorecard popup.
The quadrant reflects location, not execution: a "Cash Cow" is outperforming its location ceiling and a "Question Mark" has headroom — neither label alone judges how well the store is run.

This is one of three complementary lenses, each answering a different question — not competing verdicts: Sales × Location (this view) = is a store capturing its catchment? · Peer-group Stars/Cash Cows (Excel report) = how does it rank vs similar stores? · Intangible (Proven Performer / Structural Laggard) = is performance explained or unexplained? For the single recommended action per store, use Primary Action (Store Scorecard).

Stars - High Sales & High Location Potential (Best performers in prime locations)
Question Marks - Low Sales but High Location Potential (Optimization targets)
Cash Cows - High Sales but Low Location Potential (Overperforming their location)
Problem Stores - Low Sales & Low Location Potential (Consider relocation)

Store Scorecard

Click any row to expand store details, top opportunities, and category benchmarks. Note: Primary Action is the authoritative recommendation (relative to the store’s own location baseline). Quadrant is a second lens — absolute portfolio position (sales × location vs the medians) — so the two can differ for the same store by design; act on Primary Action. Location Potential is an average-run baseline, not a hard ceiling — well-run stores out-earn it. Per-lever upsides overlap and do not sum to the store total.

Columns are split into Controllable Levers (your upside — shown even where acting on it is hard) and Market Profile (catchment / footfall / POI / competition — location context you don't control). Click any score to see its variables.

Voice of Customer — Aspect-Based Sentiment (Google reviews)

Every Google review is parsed for which aspects customers raise (mention-share, %) and how positively they speak about each (net sentiment, −1 to +1). Mention-share is the high-variance signal — it shows what customers actually care about; a low net-sentiment on a frequently-mentioned aspect is a real pain point. The headline document-level label is ~98% positive (saturated), so this aspect view is where the signal lives.

Portfolio by aspect

Per-store aspect heatmap

Aspects mapped to the customer journey; net sentiment saturates near +0.9 for well-run aspects, so weight attention by mention-share and by the negative outliers. Stores with no/low review volume show blanks.

Product Mix & Cross-sell

Category share of each store's trailing-12-month sales vs the portfolio. A store well below the portfolio on a category is an under-penetrated cross-sell opportunity (assuming comparable catchment); well above = a proven playbook to copy.

Per-store category share (vs portfolio)

Cell = category % of the store's sales; green = over-indexed, red = under-indexed vs portfolio (≥5pp gap). Red on a big category = the cross-sell opportunity.

Site Quality — Visibility · Accessibility · Appearance

Store-by-store site-evaluation checklist scored 0–100 per bucket. Visibility and Appearance are largely controllable (signage, display, cleanliness) — low scores there are fixable. Accessibility is structural context. Cell colour = score; click a bucket header to sort.

Portfolio Playbook — what to do, ranked by total upside

One row per action, not per store: how many stores need it, the total ₹ it is worth across the portfolio, and the typical move. Click a row to see exactly which stores. Filter to a zone/city to get that owner's work queue.

Walk-in Effectiveness Funnel

How each store turns footfall into revenue: Walk-ins → acquisition mix (digital / repeat) → Conversion → Basket (ATV × UPT) → Sales per walk-in. The single best efficiency measure is Sales / walk-in — it nets conversion and basket into one number. Repeat-buyer % and CSAT show whether the experience compounds.

Cross-sell & Attach Rates

Every mattress (or anchor product) sale is a chance to attach an accessory. Attach rate = attached units ÷ anchor units over the trailing 12 months (e.g. pillows sold per mattress). A store attaching below the fleet median is leaving basket — and margin — on the table. Bars show the portfolio median per pair; the table ranks stores by a composite attach index and flags each store’s single biggest attach gap vs. fleet (the accessory to push next).

Lead-Generation & Conversion Funnel

Before a customer ever walks in, the store works a lead pipeline: leads are assigned, the call centre calls them (answer rate · effort), and they convert to store visits and then sales. The single best measure is Lead→Sale % (conversions per lead). The funnel below multiplies through — Answer rate and the two conversion steps are the levers most in the store’s control. The table ranks every store and flags its weakest funnel stage vs. fleet.

Definitions & methodology

How to read every bucket, classification and metric in this dashboard. Each store is viewed through three complementary lenses; for the single recommended next step per store, use Primary Action (Store Scorecard).

Money unit: all sales, potential, gap and uplift figures are in INR Lakhs (1 Lakhs = ₹100,000) unless a label states otherwise. Scores are 0–100 percentile-based indices, not money.

Sales × Location quadrants (this dashboard’s scatter view — is a store capturing its catchment?)
Stars
High sales and high location potential. Best performers in prime locations. Keep investing and use as templates.
Question Marks
Low sales but high location potential. The store is not yet capturing a strong catchment — the priority optimization targets.
Cash Cows
High sales but modest location potential — over-delivering for where they sit. Protect the formula; limited further headroom.
Problem Stores
Low sales and low location potential. Limited upside from the site itself — fix execution or consider relocation/exit.
Primary Action (the single recommended next step per store)
EXPAND & REPLICATE
Beats its location ceiling (>+5% vs location) through observable execution — a replicable blueprint for new sites.
PROTECT & DOCUMENT
Beats its location ceiling via unexplained factors (e.g. a strong manager or local brand pull) rather than observable levers. This edge is fragile — capture and protect what is working before it walks out the door.
MAINTAIN & OPTIMIZE
Performing in line with its location ceiling (−10% to +5%). Hold steady and fine-tune.
OPTIMIZE
Below its location ceiling (<−10%), but the gap is addressable by known levers — execute the store’s top-5 tactics.
DIAGNOSE & TURN-AROUND
Well below its location ceiling. Run the store tactics list (it recovers real value), but a large gap survives even best-case execution of every lever — so investigate the root cause in parallel (management / brand / local execution / site). Relocation or exit is a last resort, only if no cause is found.
Intangible decomposition (Store Scorecard — is performance explained by observables, or unexplained?)
Proven Performer
Strong observable fundamentals and over-delivering on them — a replicable strength.
Underdelivering Site
Good fundamentals being wasted (under-delivering what observables predict) — highest-priority fix.
Punching Above Weight
Weak fundamentals yet overachieving via intangibles — protect and learn what drives it.
Structural Laggard
Weak fundamentals and under-delivering — candidate for turnaround or exit.
Meets Expectations
Performing about as its observable fundamentals predict (a near-zero, Neutral-band intangible) — on its expected line, neither over- nor under-delivering. A store is only labelled over/under-delivering when the residual is clearly non-zero.
Ramping (New Store)
Open less than a full year, so it has not yet traded through every season. Its gap to mature peers is largely age, not execution or a poor site — so it is given no over/under-delivery verdict, and no turnaround call. The store tactics still apply; re-assess it against peers once it has traded a full year.
Key metrics
Location Potential
Model estimate (INR Lakhs) of what an average-run store would earn at this location, from catchment, POI, footfall and competition. The store’s “ceiling” reference.
Performance vs Location
% by which actual sales beat (+) or trail (−) the location potential. Outperform >+5%, underperform <−10%.
Opportunity Gap / Uplift
Realistic additional sales (INR Lakhs and %) achievable by moving controllable levers toward peer benchmarks. Capped at a realistic ceiling.
Intangible Index
0–100 score of performance unexplained by location and observable execution (50 = as expected). Above 50 = sells more than fundamentals predict. A confidence-shrunk proxy for brand / manager / loyalty, not a causal measure.
Intangible (₹)
The intangible expressed in INR Lakhs: actual sales minus location fundamentals minus observable execution, with the low-confidence portion stripped out as model uncertainty.
Unexplained Headroom
Portion of the gap to the location ceiling that known levers cannot explain — signals a root-cause investigation rather than a tactic.
